# SMS over NAS: compliance register

What this is: the requirements of this area that are built and verified against running code, the typed rows recorded while building them, and coverage counts derived from the specs (verification.md §5). Requirements are in [`requirements.md`](../../requirements.md); deviations in [`deviations.md`](../deviations.md).

Specs read: TS 24.011 j00, TS 23.040 j00, TS 23.038 j00.

Row suffixes (requirements.md): -D defect in the sim, -B a choice the spec leaves open, -G declared gap, -V deviation from a "shall", -S spec contradiction and the reading chosen, -M mutant, -T T0 reading or measurement, -F a kaluza-core defect the sim found, -X retired. Verification: U unit, KAT or oracle test; F fuzz or property test; I interop; L lab; G gate row; A real-device comparison.

| KS-SMS-T1 | 2026-10-14 | SMS tables: 24.011 j00 CP types (CP-DATA 01, CP-ACK 04, CP-ERROR 10) and RP MTIs 0-6 by direction; 23.038 j00 GSM 7-bit default alphabet (128 codes) and extension table (11). The Greek letters are Word SYMBOL fields, decoded through the Symbol font. Against pycrate: default table identical; extension identical in its 10 characters; pycrate also keeps 0x0D (CR2, 'NOTE 2: Void' in j00) and maps the reserved escape 0x1B to U+000E | spec/nas/23038/gsm7_alphabet.tsv, spec/nas/24011/*.tsv, M7 |
| KS-SMS-T2 | 2026-10-14 | M11 SMS check: CP, RP and TPDU each round-trip; every element pycrate (TS24011_PPSMS, TS23040_SMS) reads holds what ours read; tshark reads CP as gsm_a_dtap and RP as gsm_a_rp, and a TPDU inside an RP-DATA or RP-ACK built for its direction, because its dissector takes the direction from the RP layer (TS 23.040 9.2.3.1). 29 checks, all PASS | build/oracle/l3roundtrip.tsv, tests/oracles/ksimoracle/nasrt.py, M11 |
| KS-SMS-B1 | 2026-10-14 | TPDU decoding takes the direction, since TP-MTI alone does not name the type (TS 23.040 9.2.3.1), and for a report whether the carrying RP message is an RP-ERROR (TP-FCS present, 9.2.2.1a, 9.2.2.2a). TP-PI follows 9.2.3.27: a further TP-PI octet while bit 8 is set; a reserved bit set announces octets after TP-UD, which are kept as discarded rather than rejected; TP-UDL without TP-DCS means the default alphabet. GSM 7-bit packing follows TS 23.038 6.1.2.1, with fill bits after a user data header; a character outside the default alphabet and its extension table is an error, not a substitution | src/codec/nas/sms.hpp, tests/unit/nas/sms_test.cpp, M11 |
| KS-SMS-S1 | 2026-10-15 | RP-Destination Address in an MO RP-DATA (L7). TS 24.011 j00 gives two bounds: Table 7.5 lists the element as LV of 1-12 octets (so a length octet of 0-11), while 8.2.5.2 says that in the mobile station to network direction the length octet is at least 2 and at most 11. The sim follows 8.2.5.2, the clause that states the direction: RP-DA is the service centre address from EF.SMSP (TS 31.102 4.2.27, TS-Service Centre Address), its length octet 2-11; a card whose EF.SMSP holds no service centre address makes the UE refuse the MO submission locally (an event and exit code 6) instead of sending an empty RP-DA, which is what UERANSIM does (kaluza-core SMS-SC14 relays such an RP-DATA leniently). kaluza-core's own decoder bounds the length octet 2-11 too (its SMS-C08), so both sides read 8.2.5.2 alike | spec/3gpp/24/24011-j00 7.3.1.2 Table 7.5, 8.2.5.2; kaluza-core docs/compliance/smsf/codec.md SMS-C08, smsc.md SMS-SC14 (read only); requirements L7; P1 N0 |
| KS-SMS-B2 | 2026-10-15 | SMS over NAS in the UE as built in P1 N13 (src/proc/ue/sms; TS 24.011, TS 23.040, TS 24.501 5.4.5). Choices: (1) TC1* 10 s with two retransmissions (5.3.2.1 leaves the value and 1-3 retransmissions to the implementation), TR1M 40 s, TRAM 30 s (10.1); (2) one MO RP transaction at a time; a further one goes in place of the final CP-ACK of the last (5.4); (3) RP-DA is EF.SMSP's TS-Service-Centre-Address (TON/NPI and digits, record 1, 4.2.27); without one it goes empty and the event says so (L7); (4) an MT SMS-DELIVER is stored in the first free EF.SMS record (status 03, the RP-OA, the TPDU) and answered with RP-ACK without a DELIVER-REPORT; with no free record or the memory set full, RP-ERROR #22 and EF.SMSS's flag set, RP-SMMA once available; (5) TP-MR one up from EF.SMSS's last; (6) a text that does not fit one TPDU is cut into parts of 153 septets or 67 UCS2 characters with the 8-bit reference concatenation element, an escaped GSM character never split; (7) SMS-SUBMIT is refused locally (ksim-ctl exit 6) while SMS over NAS is not allowed | src/proc/ue/sms/sms.cpp; tests/procedure/sms_test.cpp |
